scope: Repository baseline gallery and collected-artwork inventory; not a census of all British Columbia visual identities. No external source content was newly verified by this audit.
methodology: Read generated collectedData.js at the baseline commit.
Count assets as source-file records; count collected designs as assets without variantOf; count full gallery entries from GALLERY_COLLECTIONS.
For missing-artwork counts, exclude bodies with existingCollection even when their collected-assets list is empty.
Compare exact path/shape attributes and inherited transforms, then resolve fills from class CSS, inline style and inheritance for palette candidates.
Inspect selected rendered candidates side by side to distinguish colour variants from changes in composition.
Verify all 208 baseline source-file SHA-256 digests, and compare every public/identity-collected SVG with catalogued files/downloads.

knownMissingEras.label: Beside the oval crest
knownMissingEras.note: An oval ministry crest — British Columbia and Forests, Lands and Natural Resource Operations around an eagle, two conifers, a deer and a fish over water — then “BCTS” in a heavy green sans over “BC Timber Sales”: a sans redrawing of the wordmark, on the covers of its business plans.

knownMissingEras.label: The worker-protection emblem
knownMissingEras.note: The board’s history describes a new design in 1968 built on protecting the worker. No picture of it has been found, so it is not drawn.

sources.title: WorkSafeBC, “Our story: 1967–1991” [S2]
sources.locator: a worker-protection logo in 1968; provincial imagery added in 1983; “Workmen’s” became “Workers’” in 1974

knownMissingEras.label: BC Rail operating identity
knownMissingEras.note: The public BC Rail name dates to 19 June 1984. The familiar red-and-blue graphic must be dated separately: later caboose research distinguishes white lettering in 1985 and a red-and-blue herald in 1986–1987 schemes. The supporting photograph below documents the latter graphic on locomotives on 21 July 1990. A verified isolated master is still sought.

sources.title: Canadian Rail 547, March–April 2012
sources.locator: Printed p.49 / PDF p.5: BC Rail name date; p.70 / PDF p.26: BCR dogwood; p.72 / PDF p.28: red-blue BC Rail graphic

sources.title: The Cariboo 23, January 1996; Ron Tuff, B.C.R.'s Wide Vision Cabooses, diagrams Greg M. Kennelly

keepDistinct.reason: The SVG and EPS have different symbol scale, corner shape and lettering arrangement. They are not merely different download formats.
The raster source is a horizontal lockup; the held SVG is stacked. Keep the horizontal reference until that layout is recovered as vector.
The raster tagline sits below BCIB; the SVG tagline sits at its right. The mobile raster omits the full-name extension. Preserve these layouts.
The 2004 raster uses large LWBC serif initials and small full name; the 2002 SVG spells out the name in italic type.
The 2003 raster is a tall stacked BC/Buildings/Corporation mark; the 2005 vector is horizontal bcbc with a tagline.
The source metadata explicitly distinguishes the earlier corporate-name raster from the 2009 short-name vector. Do not consolidate by organization name alone.
The coloured SVG intentionally includes a photograph in the disc and is correctly classified isVector=false. The white EPS is pure vector; recolouring it cannot recover that photographic treatment.

limitations: The 103 unheld records are research gaps, not proof those bodies had a separate logo.
Raster-only counts describe collected body records, not whether a related family collection has supplied/reconstructed art.
Geometry and resolved-style comparisons establish palette equivalence for listed files, not authorization for arbitrary brand recolouring.
Knowledge Network EPS geometry and colour validation is handled separately by the parent task.
